TikTok could play an important role in promoting Nepal's tourism sector and showcasing its diverse attractions to a global audience, Minister for Information and Communications Bikram Timilsina said at the launch of a collaborative campaign between Nepal Tourism Board (NTB) and TikTok.

Timilsina said the initiative would not only help expand Nepal's tourism outreach internationally but also encourage technology transfer.

title: Highland fashion show highlights Bajura wool - The Rising Nepal
description: Highland fashion show highlights Bajura wool  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
By A Staff Reporter,Kathmandu, Nov. 7: Lamasim Hill in Porkhe Lek, Bajura, turned into an open-air fashion runway as models showcased garments made from local sheep wool at an event aimed at promoting tourism and supporting Himalayan farmers.

Held nearly 3,000 metres above sea level beneath Badimalika, the event, titled ‘Threads of the Himalaya: Farm to Fashion,’ brought together local wool producers, designers, artists and models. It aimed to connect Bajura’s sheep farmers with international markets and promote the Badimalika region as a tourism destination.

The event was jointly organised by the Threads of the Himalaya Foundation and KASA, a Nepali fashion brand seeking to expand into international markets. A 55-member team travelled from Kathmandu to Bajura for the event.

BBC MasterChef Santosh Shah participated to showcase Nepali cuisine, while former Minister for Women, Children and Senior Citizens Shraddha Shrestha also attended the event.

More than three dozen artistes and models, including Shweta Khadka, former Miss Nepal Ashmi Shrestha, Niti Shah, Bhawana Pant and Ayushman Deshraj Joshi, walked the runway wearing garments made from Bajura’s sheep wool. The designs combined local craftsmanship with contemporary fashion.

Tourism entrepreneur Janesh Bhandari said the initiative aimed to make better use of wool that often goes to waste or is sold at low prices. He said the project would help connect local production with international markets while linking Badimalika’s tourism with economic opportunities for local communities.

Bajura has more than 70,000 sheep, while neighbouring Bajhang and Darchula also have significant potential for wool production.

Former finance minister Naresh Kumar Shahi recalled carrying 13 sacks of wool from Kolti to Kathmandu to demonstrate the potential of local products. He said Bajura’s wool could meet international standards and that combining trade and tourism could improve the livelihoods of farmers.

The organisers plan to collect wool from Bajura and neighbouring districts and establish a wool-processing centre in Bajura. The centre is expected to create jobs for young people and help turn sheep farming into a more sustainable and commercially viable livelihood.

title: Nepal to open World Cup Qualifier Play-Off against Italy - The Rising Nepal
description: Nepal to open World Cup Qualifier Play-Off against Italy  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
By A Staff Reporter, Kathmandu, Nov. 7: Nepal will launch their ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup Qualifier Play-off campaign against Italy on home soil, following the release of the official tournament schedule by the International Cricket Council (ICC) on Friday.

The eight-team round-robin tournament will take place in Kathmandu from 4 to 21 December. The top four sides will advance to the final ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup Qualifier 2027.

Fixtures will be staged simultaneously at the Tribhuvan University (TU) Cricket Ground in Kirtipur and the Mulpani Cricket Ground.

Hosts Nepal will play all seven of their matches at the TU Cricket Ground. The host nation are joined in the Play-off by Canada, Namibia, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), who finished in the bottom four of Cricket World Cup League 2, alongside Italy, Jersey, Kuwait, and Uganda, who progressed via the ICC Challenge League.

Following their opener against Italy, Nepal face Uganda on 6 December, the UAE on 10 December, Jersey on 12 December, Canada on 14 December, Namibia on 18 December, and Kuwait in their final match on 21 December.

Ireland and the West Indies have already secured spots in the Global Qualifier as the top two ranked nations outside the eight automatic qualifiers, excluding Full Member co-hosts South Africa and Zimbabwe. The Netherlands, Oman, Scotland, and the USA earned direct entry to the Global Qualifier after finishing in the top four of League 2.

Welcoming the fixture announcement, ICC General Manager of Events and Operations Gaurav Saxena highlighted the importance of the event.

"The Qualifier Play-off is a crucial stage in the pathway to the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup 2027, and I am sure all eight teams will be eager to seize this opportunity to secure a place in the next stage," Saxena said.

"Associate cricket is vital to the continued growth and global development of our sport. Competitions such as this provide teams with valuable opportunities to showcase their talent, gain experience, and raise their standards."

At the Global Qualifier, the tournament winner will gain direct entry into the World Cup group stage, while the teams finishing second, third, and fourth will progress to a newly introduced Super Series to contend for the remaining places.

The ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup 2027 will feature 14 teams competing across 57 matches in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia from 2 October to 21 November 2027.

title: Minister Badi visits Raute settlement in Salyan - The Rising Nepal
description: Minister Badi visits Raute settlement in Salyan  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
By Pratik Ichchhuk Sharma, alyan, Nov. 7: The endangered Raute community has urged the government to ensure food supplies, safe housing and livelihood opportunities.

Minister for Women, Children, Gender and Sexual Minorities and Social Security Sita Badi, who visited the Raute settlement at Namra in Bangad Kupinde Municipality-1, Salyan, pledged to take initiatives to address the community's demands.

During her visit, Minister Badi met and held discussions with members of the Raute community. She also interacted with children to learn about their living conditions, problems and needs.

During the discussion, Raute Chief Dil Bahadur Shahi requested the government to provide food and other essential daily necessities to the community. Similarly, Raute young woman Samjhana Shahi urged the government to ensure that they could live in safe housing like other citizens. Another community member, Gajali Shahi, also drew attention to the various problems faced by the community and called for initiatives to address them. Minister Badi said she would take initiatives to ensure a market for and purchase of wooden products made by the Raute community using their traditional skills. She pledged to prioritise the community's problems and needs and incorporate them into future plans and programmes.

Expressing concern over the living conditions of Raute children and other community members, she said she would coordinate with the concerned authorities to address the challenges they face in their daily lives.

For the health, sanitation and social integration of the Raute community, Social Service Centre (SOSEC) Nepal has mobilised four personnel, including two health workers and two social mobilisers. SOSEC Nepal Chairman Hira Singh Thapa said the organisation had been working in the areas of healthcare and social protection for the community.

A total of 130 Rautes, comprising 71 females and 59 males, currently live in the settlement at Namra in Bangad Kupinde Municipality-1. Of them, 51 are children and 23 are single women, according to the details provided.

Welcoming Minister Badi to their settlement, Raute children also presented her with a token of love bearing her name. In recent years, Raute children have shown growing interest in literacy.

title: Marigold farming flourishes in Lamjung - The Rising Nepal
description: Marigold farming flourishes in Lamjung  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
By Our Correspondent, Lamjung, Nov. 7: Marigold farming has expanded in Lamjung district this year, with a growing number of farmers taking up flower cultivation. In previous years, only two or three farmers were engaged in the business, but many more have joined the sector this year.

Farmers said marigold flowers blooming during the Tihar season have not only enhanced the beauty of their surroundings but also increased their income.

Interestingly, four journalists from the district have also taken up marigold farming this year. Having spent years reporting on people's stories and hardships, they are now putting their own sweat into the soil, seeking to make commercial flower cultivation a source of income and self-reliance.

Despite their busy schedules in journalism, flower farming has emerged as an attractive agricultural venture for them. Their fields, now covered with blooming marigolds, have added colour to the landscape while opening up new avenues of income.

Nabin Raj Kuinkel, Lamjung correspondent for the national daily Gorkhapatra, has been cultivating marigolds on four ropanis of land in Targaun, Marsyangdi Rural Municipality-9. He has been continuing flower farming for the past four years through his Marsyangdi Agriculture Farm, where he has constructed 15 polyhouses.

Similarly, Milan Sharma Danai, publisher and editor of the weekly Lamjung Aawaj; Santosh Poudel, editor of the weekly Lamjung Patra; and Birat Neupane, associate editor of Laxminarayan HD, have also taken up marigold farming this year. Danai has cultivated flowers in Gaunsahar, Besishahar Municipality-3, while Poudel and Neupane have grown them in Duradanda, Sundarbazaar Municipality-4.

Journalist Danai said his first experience of flower farming had provided him with both valuable lessons and encouragement. He added that he had supplied flower garlands and loose flowers to Besishahar, as well as to Manang and Kathmandu.

Journalist Poudel has combined flower cultivation with beekeeping. He said he was selling both flower garlands and honey during the current season.

Buddhi Ale of Gahate, Sundarbazaar, has also continued flower farming. Similarly, Prasanna Kuinkel, proprietor of Marsyangdi Agro Concern in Marsyangdi Rural Municipality-9, is engaged in the business.

Farmer Ivan Joshi of Samibhanjyang, Madhyanepal Municipality-5, said flower farming had proved a promising venture. He added that he had received substantial demand for flowers and garlands from Pokhara and Damauli.

Joshi urged the government to introduce policies and support programmes to make Nepal self-sufficient in flower production.

"There is plenty of fallow land in villages. The government should support farmers in utilising such land for flower cultivation," he said.

According to Joshi, demand for flowers rises sharply during Tihar, often making it difficult for local farmers to meet the market requirements. Farmers said flower garlands were also in demand for programmes organised by government and non-governmental offices throughout the year.

Agricultural experts said flower farming could generate higher returns with lower investment compared to vegetables and other food crops.

Madan Regmi, an economic expert at the Agriculture Development Office, Lamjung, said farmers could avoid market-related difficulties by cultivating flowers alongside other crops.

Farmers sold marigold flowers at prices ranging from Rs. 300 to Rs. 500 per kg this year. They said they were satisfied with the prices received.

title: Supreme Court registers Karki’s petition for reinstatement as Nepal Police chief - The Kathmandu Post
description: Supreme Court registers Karki’s petition for reinstatement as Nepal Police chief  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Sacked Nepal Police chief Dan Bahadur Karki has challenged the government’s decision to remove him and appoint Manoj Kumar KC as inspector general, appealing the Supreme Court to reinstate him and suspend the new chief’s authority pending a final verdict.

The Supreme Court registered Karki’s writ petition on Friday after keeping it under preliminary review for a day. The hearing has been scheduled for November 16.

Karki has sought the annulment of the Cabinet decision transferring him to the newly created post of prime minister’s special security adviser and appointing KC as police chief. Karki has also sought an interim order allowing him to resume his duties while barring KC from exercising the powers of inspector general.

In his petition, Karki cites two Supreme Court precedents involving the removal of senior officials from their positions: the case of former police chief Achyut Krishna Kharel, who was removed in 1997, and that of Hitendra Dev Shakya, the former executive director of the Nepal Electricity Authority who was transferred to the Water and Energy Commission.

Karki argues that the government’s decision in his case was unlawful because it did not cite any legal provision authorising the removal of a serving inspector general or his transfer to a post outside the police organisation.

He says neither the Police Act 1955 nor the Police Regulations 2014 provides for the transfer of an incumbent IG to a position created within the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers.

Kharel precedent

Karki has relied heavily on the Supreme Court’s ruling in the case involving Kharel, who was removed as inspector general on April 3, 1997, just 36 days after taking office.

The then home minister, Bamdev Gautam, transferred Kharel to the post of chief of the National Investigation Department and appointed Dhruba Bahadur Pradhan as police chief.

Kharel challenged the decision in the Supreme Court. A special bench comprising justices Hari Prasad Sharma, Indra Raj Pandey and Bhairav Prasad Lamsal ruled that the government’s decision lacked a proper basis and was motivated by political considerations.

The court held that the police chief’s appointment was not a political appointment that could be changed simply because the government had changed. It also warned that arbitrary changes in police leadership could undermine the morale, professional independence and effectiveness of the force.

Although the law allowed police officers to be appointed to the National Investigation Department, the court said that authority could not be used without a reasonable basis to remove an incumbent inspector general.

The court found that the government’s decision to appoint Kharel to the department’s top post was arbitrary and lacked justification. It also said the decision appeared to have been made solely to promote Pradhan, without explaining the reasons or necessity for doing so.

Karki argues that the circumstances of his removal are even more problematic because, unlike in Kharel’s case, the government has not identified any legal provision allowing it to transfer an incumbent IGP to the newly created advisory position.

Shakya precedent

Karki has also cited the Supreme Court’s ruling in the case of Shakya, who was transferred from his position as executive director of the Nepal Electricity Authority to an expert member’s post at the Water and Energy Commission.

The petition argues that the court had made it clear that appointing someone to another position and removing them from their existing post are legally distinct actions.

It cites the court’s reasoning that an official cannot be considered to have left their original position simply because they have been appointed to another post, unless the appointment was made with their consent.

The petition says the principle applies to Karki’s case, arguing that the government cannot indirectly remove him from the police chief’s position by assigning him to another post.

No hearing or consultation

Karki also argues that the government violated the principles of natural justice by removing him without informing him of the reasons, seeking an explanation or giving him an opportunity to respond.

In his petition, Karki says he was not consulted before the Cabinet decided to appoint him the prime minister’s special security adviser, nor was his consent obtained.

Karki says he knew about his removal through the media and subsequently received a letter from the secretary at the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Karki argues that the government should have shown him the grounds for his removal and provided an opportunity to defend himself before taking the decision.

He has asked the court to annul the Cabinet decision, arguing that the failure to follow due process makes it unlawful.

The petition also challenges the government’s reliance on Section 9(2) of the Police Act 1955, which puts police personnel’s tenure at the government’s discretion.

Karki says the Supreme Court’s ruling in the Kharel case made it clear that this provision cannot be exercised arbitrarily or used to justify the removal of the serving police chief without objective grounds.

Petition seeks reinstatement

Karki’s petition challenges the Cabinet’s November 4 decision to remove him, appoint him as the prime minister’s special security adviser and promote KC to inspector general.

KC assumed office on Wednesday after receiving his insignia.

Karki argues that the three decisions were part of a single process designed to remove him unlawfully and install a replacement.

He says the government has not cited any shortcomings in his performance, conduct, ability or qualifications to justify the decision.

The petition seeks the annulment of the Cabinet decision transferring Karki to the advisory post, as well as the decision promoting KC and all subsequent actions, including his appointment and the awarding of insignia.

It also asks the court to determine under what legal authority KC is holding the position of inspector general.

Karki has sought a mandamus order directing the government to restore him to the post for the remainder of his tenure under Rule 127 of the Police Regulations 2014, along with his previous legal status, records, salary, allowances and other service benefits.

He has also requested a prohibitory order preventing the government from removing him, transferring him elsewhere, retiring him before the end of his tenure or appointing another person as police chief without following the law and prescribed procedures.

Karki argues that restoring him to his original position would not cause any harm to the government or other respondents, while allowing the disputed decision to stand would undermine his rights.

Registration delayed by a day

Karki’s lawyer, Tik Bahadur Kunwar, submitted the writ petition to the Supreme Court at 10:30 am on Thursday, the day after the government announced its decision.

The court administration kept the petition under preliminary review throughout the day.

Supreme Court spokesperson Ashok Kumar Chhetri and chief registrar Bimal Paudel were attending a UNDP event on Thursday, contributing to the delay in reviewing the petition, according to the report.

The petition was registered on Friday, pushing the hearing beyond the Tihar festival.

Thagindra Kattel, registrar at the Supreme Court, said the hearing had been scheduled for November 16 at the petitioner’s request.

What happens at the first hearing?

The first hearing on November 16 will take place before a single bench is assigned through a lottery.

The court has two options.

It could issue an interim order directing the government to maintain the status quo and suspend implementation of the Cabinet decision. If it does so, the court may summon both sides for further discussion. Karki would then return to his previous position, while KC would be barred from exercising the powers of inspector general.

Alternatively, the court could issue a show-cause order asking the government to explain its decision and summon both parties for a hearing on whether an interim order should be issued.

In that situation, no immediate interim order would be in place, allowing KC to continue as police chief while Karki would remain out of office.

title: Kala Sahitya Dot Com releases collections of poems - The Rising Nepal
description: Kala Sahitya Dot Com releases collections of poems  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
By A Staff Reporter,Kathmandu, Nov. 7: Poets from Nepal and abroad recited their poetry during an event organised by the Nepali Kala and Sahitya Dot Com Foundation in Kathmandu.

Guest poets Dinesh Adhikari from Nepal, alongside Slovenian poets Brane Mozetic, Blaz Bozic, and Veronika Razpotnik, recited their creations. Similarly, poets Laxman Gamnage, Hemchandra Nepal, Anita Lama, Rajendra Shalabh, Badri Pokharel, Gita Karki, Krishna Raj DC, Viplav Dhakal, Phulman Bal, Babu Tripathi, and Rajani Mila also read out their poems.

During the event, several publications of the Foundation were launched. Along with the Foundation's annual publication Kalashree Sahitya yearly, three translated poetry collections—China: Shaswat Aawaj (a compilation of contemporary Chinese poems), Nigeria: Shaswat Aawaj (a collection of Nigerian poems translated into Nepali), and Slovenia: Shaswat Aawaj (a collection of Slovenian poems)—were released. An e-magazine was also unveiled at the event.

The 'Nepal Award 2026', presented to foreign creators who contribute to the promotion and enrichment of Nepali language and literature, was conferred on Slovenian poet Brane Mozetic. Additionally, the 'NLG Kalashree Srijana Award 2083' was awarded to poet Pradeep Bhattarai from Kohalpur.

Literary figure SP Koirala remarked that the Foundation has consistently conducted distinguished cultural and literary endeavours, emphasising that art and literature heighten human consciousness.

Chief Patron of the Foundation Dr. Bimal Koirala highlighted the organisation’s ongoing initiatives and commended the poetic craft of the visiting international poets. Bimal Wagle, Chairperson of NLG, stated that their institution has continuously supported the upliftment of Nepali art and literature.

Chairperson of the Foundation Momila Joshi shared that the organisation actively works towards the advancement of Nepali language and literature. Reflecting on the effort behind these initiatives, she mentioned that they undertake such endeavours for pure artistic fulfilment, while also speaking about the translation of poetry and highlighting Chinese, Slovenian, and Nigerian poets and their literary works.

During the event, translator of the published works Keshab Sigdel and Liu Zhanping, Deputy Director of the China Cultural Centre, also shared their reflections.

Arguments of the plaintiff

According to his position, neither the 1955 Police Act nor the 2014 Police Regulations provide for such a transfer.

The former police chief also said that the decision was made without notification of the reasons, a request for explanations, or an opportunity to respond to the allegations. According to him, he learned about his removal from the media and later received a letter from the secretary of the Ministry of Home Affairs.

In addition, the plaintiff mentioned the case of Hitendra Dev Shakya, former executive director of the Nepal Electricity Authority. In that case, the court stated that appointing an official to another position does not automatically terminate their authority in the previous position without their consent.

title: Economic Digest: A Snapshot of Nepal’s Business News - Khabarhub
description: Economic Digest: A Snapshot of Nepal’s Business News  Khabarhub
publisher.title: Khabarhub
full_article:
KATHMANDU: Economic Digest presents a brief yet comprehensive roundup of major business developments in Nepal, delivered in clear and accessible summaries.

Nepal’s economic landscape presents a mixed picture, with modest financial market gains, infrastructure investment progress and persistent structural challenges affecting businesses and consumers. The NEPSE index edged up 2.64 points to 2,655.22, supported by positive market breadth and Rs 3.46 billion in turnover, while the proposed 7.18 percent dividend from Mahalaxmi Development Bank and a 342.6 percent rise in Reliance Spinning Mills’ quarterly profit indicate encouraging corporate performance. However, declining gold and silver prices reflect a softer domestic precious metals market.

Infrastructure development remains a major priority, with progress on the Arun-III and Upper Karnali hydropower projects and renewed preparations for the Janakpurdham-Ayodhya railway link offering prospects for energy production, tourism and cross-border economic activity. Nepal’s engagement with the European Union also highlights the importance of export diversification as the country approaches graduation from least developed country status.

Nevertheless, persistent structural weaknesses remain evident. Poor road connectivity has pushed essential commodity prices in remote Gorkha settlements to several times their official rates, while smuggled Indian marigolds threaten domestic floriculture. Meanwhile, loan recovery measures, trekking permit enforcement and improved airport services underscore growing attention to financial discipline, regulatory compliance and service delivery.

Overall, sustainable economic growth will depend on translating investment commitments into completed infrastructure, strengthening domestic production, improving market access and addressing regional disparities in economic opportunity.

NEPSE gains 2.64 points as turnover reaches Rs 3.46 billion

The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) index edged up 2.64 points to close at 2,655.22 on Friday, recording a modest gain amid fluctuations throughout the trading session. The benchmark index reached an intraday high of 2,662 points before settling in positive territory at the close. A total of 10.7 million shares of 336 companies were traded through 33,215 transactions, generating a turnover of Rs 3.46 billion. Market breadth remained positive, with share prices of 158 companies advancing, while 107 declined. The prices of 14 companies remained unchanged. Most sectoral indices closed higher, although the ‘Others’ group recorded a marginal decline. Crest Micro Life Insurance emerged as the top gainer, with its share price climbing 14.08 percent to Rs 1,192 per share. Meanwhile, Ghorahi Cement recorded the highest transaction value, with shares worth more than Rs 216.3 million traded during the session.

Gold price falls Rs 5,900 per tola, silver drops to Rs 3,810

Gold and silver prices declined in the domestic market on Friday, with hallmark gold losing Rs 5,900 per tola and silver falling by Rs 110 per tola. According to the Federation of Nepal Gold and Silver Dealers’ Association, hallmark gold is being traded at Rs 283,000 per tola (11.66 grams), down from Rs 288,900 on Thursday. Similarly, the price of silver has decreased to Rs 3,810 per tola from Rs 3,920 a day earlier, marking a decline of Rs 110. The latest adjustment reflects a downward movement in the domestic precious metals market.

NOC depots to remain open during Tihar holidays

Nepal Oil Corporation (NOC) has decided to keep its depots and provincial offices operational during the Tihar holidays, including public holidays, to ensure an uninterrupted supply of petroleum products. The decision has been taken in view of consumer demand and to facilitate the smooth distribution of petroleum products during the festive period. According to NOC spokesperson Manoj Kumar Thakur, depots and provincial offices in Biratnagar, Amlekhgunj, Thankot, Pokhara, Bhairahawa, Surkhet, Dhangadhi, Nepalgunj, Dang, Janakpur, Charali, Birgunj and Dipayal will remain open as required based on local demand. The Corporation said the arrangement would help ensure the availability of petroleum products and minimise inconvenience to consumers during the festival holidays.

Investment Board reports progress in major hydropower and infrastructure projects

Investment Board Nepal (IBN) has reported significant progress in the physical construction and financial management of several major hydropower and infrastructure projects following its periodic review of ongoing developments. Physical construction of the 900-megawatt Arun-III Hydroelectric Project has crossed 77 percent, while progress on its transmission line construction has exceeded 60 percent. The project is targeting commercial electricity generation by mid-March 2027. Similarly, financial management documents worth Rs 163 billion have been secured for the 900-megawatt Upper Karnali Hydropower Project, with construction expected to begin within four years. Investment approvals have also been finalised for the Nar Khola and Sani Bheri-3 hydropower projects, valued at Rs 10.75 billion and Rs 10.42 billion, respectively. The board has also expanded its single-window service facilities to simplify administrative procedures and improve services for investors.

Immigration Department fines travel agency and four Mexican nationals for unauthorised trekking

The Department of Immigration has fined a registered travel agency and four Mexican nationals for undertaking unauthorised trekking activities in the restricted area of Lower Dolpa in violation of Nepal’s immigration and tourism regulations. Acting on investigation reports submitted by the District Administration Office, Dolpa, the department imposed a fine of Rs 50,000 on Mount Rose Tours and Travels Private Limited under Section 10(4) of the Immigration Act, 1992. Each of the four foreign nationals was also fined Rs 10,000 and required to pay an additional restricted-area permit fee of USD 20. The department has reiterated the need for strict compliance with permit requirements and regulations governing travel and trekking in restricted areas.

Salt prices reach Rs 200 per packet in remote Chumnubri due to poor road access

Residents of remote settlements in Chumnubri Rural Municipality, Gorkha, are being forced to pay as much as Rs 200 for a packet of iodised salt due to the lack of road connectivity and high transportation costs. Although the Salt Trading Corporation has fixed the base price at Rs 26 per packet, transportation difficulties and reliance on mules to carry essential supplies have pushed retail prices sharply higher. The cost of transporting goods between Pangsing and Samdo alone reaches Rs 100 per kilogram. Residents of Samdo and Samagaun are paying Rs 200 per packet, while those in Lho and Chhule are paying between Rs 150 and Rs 200. Although government subsidies cover transportation costs up to Sirdibas in Ward No. 3, settlements in the upper mountainous areas remain outside the subsidy arrangement. The prolonged delay in completing the Benighat-Arughat-Larke road project has further compounded transportation difficulties, leaving residents across six remote wards struggling with high prices of essential commodities.

Industry minister highlights EU support for expanding Nepali exports

Minister for Industry, Commerce and Supplies Deepak Kumar Shah has highlighted the importance of continued cooperation with the European Union (EU) in expanding market access and diversifying exports of Nepali manufactured products. Speaking at an event in Kathmandu marking the 25th anniversary of the EU’s Everything But Arms (EBA) trade preference initiative, Shah reaffirmed the government’s commitment to addressing practical trade barriers and strengthening the country’s export capacity. EU Ambassador to Nepal Charles Whiteley praised the craftsmanship and distinctive products of Nepali enterprises, emphasising their potential in international markets. The Federation of Export Entrepreneurs Nepal also stressed the need for continued dialogue and cooperation between Nepal and the EU, particularly as the country prepares to graduate from its least developed country (LDC) status.

Smuggled Indian marigolds worth Rs 5.9 million seized in Morang and Jhapa

The illegal import of marigold flowers from India has raised concerns among domestic floriculturists ahead of Tihar, with authorities seizing smuggled flowers worth Rs 5.9 million from cold storage facilities in Morang and Jhapa. Local flower producers say the influx of cheaper Indian flowers is threatening domestic production and undermining their investment in floriculture. Ramkumar Rajbanshi, a floriculturist from Naya Bazar, Katahari-4, Morang, said he had invested approximately Rs 1.2 million in cultivating marigolds on around 2.709 hectares of land, employing 20 to 25 workers daily. Rajbanshi, who supplies flowers to Biratnagar, Morang, Sunsari, Jhapa and Kathmandu, said he had already suffered losses after approximately 1,000 kilograms of flowers were damaged by rainfall. He called on the authorities to strengthen border monitoring to control illegal imports. Similarly, a group led by Kavita Basnet in Shivasatakshi Municipality-10, Jhapa, has invested in cultivating marigolds, targeting an income of Rs 300,000 from 10,000 plants grown on 2,031.77 square metres of land. The group has also expressed concern over competition from smuggled flowers. The Armed Police Force Nepal’s No. 3 Battalion Headquarters, Kankalini, Morang, led by Superintendent of Police Gehendra Bahadur Bhandari, seized the smuggled flowers from cold storage facilities in the two districts. Despite domestic production meeting an estimated 80 to 85 percent of demand during Tihar, illegal imports continue to pose challenges for local producers.

Tribhuvan International Airport introduces live video feeds of baggage handling

Tribhuvan International Airport has introduced a live video monitoring system in its international arrival baggage claim area, allowing passengers to watch the handling of their luggage in real time. The facility enables arriving passengers to view live footage of baggage handling, from the aircraft’s cargo hold to the conveyor belts in the arrival terminal. The initiative has been introduced following ministerial directives, with the objective of improving transparency, enhancing passenger convenience and reducing uncertainty over baggage handling. Airport authorities expect the system to help passengers monitor the movement of their luggage while strengthening accountability and improving the quality of ground-handling services. The initiative is also part of broader efforts to modernise airport services and improve the passenger experience in line with international aviation standards.

Janakpurdham-Ayodhya railway link advances with technical inspection

Preparations for a proposed railway connection between Janakpurdham in Nepal and Ayodhya in India have moved forward following a technical inspection involving a 17-coach train at Kurtha Railway Station in Dhanusha. The train, accompanied by Indian Railway officials and operating under locomotive number WDP-4D 40370, arrived from Ayodhya on Thursday for preliminary technical assessments. The inspection focused on railway infrastructure, track capacity, operational safety and technical readiness for the proposed cross-border service. Nepal Railway Company said preliminary tests and inspections had been conducted as part of preparations for the service. However, formal bilateral agreements covering the commencement date, security arrangements and administrative procedures are yet to be finalised. Business leaders in Janakpurdham expect the proposed railway connection to boost religious tourism, hospitality businesses and cross-border trade by facilitating travel between the two important religious destinations. They have also called for streamlined immigration procedures and improved customs facilities to ensure the service operates smoothly and delivers economic benefits to the region.

Mahalaxmi Development Bank proposes 7.18 percent dividend for FY 2025/26

Mahalaxmi Development Bank Limited has proposed a total dividend of 7.18 percent from its profits for the fiscal year 2025/26. A meeting of the bank’s board of directors, the 657th of its kind, decided to recommend a dividend comprising 3.40 percent bonus shares and 3.78 percent cash dividends, including applicable taxes. Based on the bank’s paid-up capital of Rs 4.511 billion, the proposed distribution includes bonus shares worth Rs 156.9 million and cash dividends amounting to Rs 170.5 million. The proposed dividend distribution is subject to approval from the relevant regulatory authorities.

Rastriya Banijya Bank gives loan defaulters 35 days to clear dues

Rastriya Banijya Bank has issued a 35-day notice to hundreds of women entrepreneurs who have defaulted on unsecured concessional loans provided under government-supported poverty alleviation programmes. In public notices issued on Friday, the state-owned bank directed the borrowers to clear their outstanding principal, interest and penalty charges within the stipulated period. The bank warned that failure to settle the dues could result in legal action, including blacklisting through the Credit Information Bureau, requests for passport cancellation, restrictions on foreign travel and the initiation of legal proceedings for asset recovery. The defaulted loans involve borrowers from various branches across the country and cover a range of small-scale enterprises, including agricultural businesses, tailoring shops, beauty salons and retail ventures established under concessional lending schemes.

Reliance Spinning Mills posts 342.6 percent profit growth in first quarter

Reliance Spinning Mills Limited has reported a sharp increase in net profit, with earnings rising 342.6 percent to Rs 304.8 million in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026/27. According to the company’s unaudited financial statements, net profit stood at Rs 68.8 million during the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year. The company’s operating revenue also increased by 28.8 percent to Rs 3.20 billion during the review period, reflecting improved business performance. Meanwhile, financial expenses declined to Rs 43.8 million, providing further support to the company’s profitability. With a paid-up capital of Rs 1.90 billion, the company reported annualised earnings per share (EPS) of Rs 63.97.

Women entrepreneurs receive leadership training in Kathmandu

The Federation of Nepalese Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FNCCI) and the Associated Women Entrepreneurs of Nepal jointly organised a leadership development workshop in Kathmandu on Friday to strengthen the managerial and professional capabilities of women entrepreneurs. The workshop, titled Self Leadership: Purpose, Power and Personal Identity, focused on developing self-awareness, improving decision-making skills and building confidence and professional resilience among women business founders. The training was facilitated by Kunduz Kachieva, an international management expert from Germany. Organisers highlighted the importance of strengthening women’s leadership, communication and management skills to support sustainable business growth and promote a more inclusive entrepreneurial environment.

Foreign Minister Khanal to lead Nepali delegation to COP31 in Türkiye

Minister for Foreign Affairs Shisir Khanal is set to leave for Antalya, Türkiye, on November 7 to lead the Nepali delegation to the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).The global climate conference is scheduled to take place from November 9 to 20. According to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister Khanal will address the opening plenary of COP31 on November 9. He will also participate in the Leaders’ Summit scheduled for November 11 and 12. During the conference, Khanal is scheduled to attend several high-level events, including Advancing the Mountain Agenda: Glaciers, Cryosphere and Resilience under Overshoot, Shared Responsibility and Sustainable Financing. The event is being jointly hosted by Nepal, Tajikistan, the Kyrgyz Republic, Bhutan and Pakistan.

title: Shining bright - Nepali Times
description: Shining bright  Nepali Times
publisher.title: Nepali Times
full_article:
Four years after its Light Up Pokhara Campaign was launched, 23 high-mast lights and 2,000 ‘smart’ streetlights were installed in the tourist city.

Since then, the Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) has put up 200 high illumination poles all over Nepal, giving cities bright night lights. But the high lumen LED lamps have dimmed the night sky, veiling views of the Milky Way, constellations and mountains glowing in the moonlight, like Mt Machapuchre from the north (main photo) that people from all over the world come to see.

Street lights make cities safer, and are a sign of progress. But many now ask how much light do cities actually need, and is there a way to confine illumination strictly to the target ground area?

Across Phewa Lake is Raniban, a densely forested slope that used to be alive with fireflies and bats at night. It is the habitat for birds, butterflies and never before classified damselflies.

The bright glow of the city now illuminates the forest, and during Pokhara's many street festivals there is the added noise of blaring music and fireworks.

“We don’t have proper urban planning so that city lights do not disturb its nature areas,” says Hum Gurung of Birdlife International, who is based in Pokhara. “High-mast lights are intensely bright and are meant for stadiums, but they are increasingly being put up in core city areas.”

Numerous studies show that light pollution at night has far-reaching biological effects on living things, including humans, disturbing their circadian rhythms and internal body clocks. Artificial light at night is no longer just a city problem. A research paper on its biological impact notes that skyglow and even vehicle headlights also affect rural areas.

On Arwa Danda 40km east of Pokhara, the local Ward decided to put up a 16m high pole with a 60,000 lumen LED lamp. No one could explain why such a bright light was needed on an isolated and heavily forested hilltop. Hum Gurung posted a photo of the light on social media with the caption: ‘The Two moons of Pokhara’.

The high-mast light at Arwa Danda as seen in the early morning. Photo: HUM GURUNG

Following this, Pokhara mayor Dhana Raj Acharya said that if the bright light was so environmentally harmful, it could be switched off after 10PM, but he never followed through. One recent full moon night, the light disturbed the spectacular view of Annapurna by night for trekkers camped nearby.

TOWERING VIEWS

Many of Nepal’s hilltops now have viewtowers to promote tourism, and putting lights on top of them is seen as a trendy way to promote tourism — forgetting that many trekkers come to Nepal to admire the night sky and mountains glowing in the moonlight.

title: Cricketer David Miller scores 93 runs on Nepal debut — Kathmandu Post - UA.NEWS
description: Cricketer David Miller scores 93 runs on Nepal debut — Kathmandu Post  UA.NEWS
publisher.title: UA.NEWS
full_article:
South African cricketer David Miller scored 93 runs off 55 balls in his debut match for Karnali Yaks in the Nepal Premier League in Kathmandu. His team lost to Sudurpaschim Royals by 39 runs, but Miller was named player of the match, Kathmandu Post reports.

Karnali Yaks were chasing a target of 177 runs and lost several wickets early. Miller came in to bat at number four with the score at 22/2, and after the powerplay the team was at 35/3. While the other Karnali Yaks players continued to lose wickets, he carefully guided the innings.

Seven sixes in his debut innings

Miller reached 50 runs off 38 balls, while his next 43 came off just 17. His tally included seven sixes, four of them in the final over. After hitting two consecutive fours in the sixth over, he did not score a boundary for nine overs before accelerating the pace.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

After the match, Miller said the pitch was slow, so in such conditions it was important to get into the right position and commit fully to the shots. He also said that the decision for him to bat at number four was made by the team management.

Karnali Yaks' upcoming matches

Karnali Yaks fast bowler Nandan Yadav said Miller's performance showed his teammates how to play on this ground and gave the bowlers much material to learn from. According to Yadav, despite his status as a global star, Miller is open to communicating with local players. Miller himself said that he also seeks to help local cricketers.

Karnali Yaks will play their next matches against Pokhara Avengers, Lumbini Lions and Chitwan Rhinos on November 9, 12 and 15, respectively. The team is close to a place in the top four.

title: Balen Shah's U-turn: Nepal PM meets top Indian diplomat months after snub - India Today
description: Balen Shah's U-turn: Nepal PM meets top Indian diplomat months after snub  India Today
publisher.title: India Today
full_article:
Around six months ago, Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah refused to meet the Indian foreign secretary, which resulted in Vikram Misri's visit being postponed. Nepalese media reports then cited Shah's reluctance to meet with foreign officials who are not of an equivalent level. On Thursday, he sat down with the very same Indian diplomat. Perhaps, this time Shah's ego had to make way for pragmatism as Nepal just cannot brush away its largest trading partner.

advertisement ❮❯

Read Full Story

On Thursday, Shah met Misri in Kathmandu as the foreign secretary wrapped up his two-day visit to the Himalayan nation. It comes ahead of the Nepal PM's visit to India later this month (November 22 likely), in what will be his first bilateral trip since assuming office in March. The decision is another major turnaround by Shah, who previously decided not to make foreign visits in his first year in office. Balen Shah's visit to India later this month will be the first visit by a Nepal PM in three years (AP)Â

BALEN SHAH MEETS FOREIGN SECY

During his meeting with Misri, Shah was seen without his usual trademark sunglasses. Perhaps taking them off helped him see the importance of ties with India more clearly. The talks focused on water resources, energy, and trade, a joint statement said.

The U-turn is striking. Around six months ago, Misri had to unexpectedly call off his two-day visit to Kathmandu in May. While no reason was provided by India, a report in The Kathmandu Post cited Shah's self-imposed rule of avoiding one-on-one meetings with foreign diplomats.

The report, which quoted government officials, framed the approach as a "new protocol" where the PM won't meet officials below the foreign minister level.

It was not just Misri. Shah also refused meetings with US assistant secretary of state Paul Kapur and US envoy to India Sergio Gor earlier this year.

In the Indian context, Misri's visit was considered important to engage with the new leadership in Kathmandu after the violent Gen Z protests last year. Apart from trade and energy ties, Nepal's unique geographical position is key to India's security.

The snub to India came as the long-running border dispute over the Kalapani-Lipulekh junction resurfaced.

The tensions compounded after India and China agreed to reopen the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra via Uttarakhand's Lipulekh Pass. Kathmandu claims Lipulekh as part of its territory under the 1816 Sugauli Treaty. India rejected Nepal's position, describing its territorial claims as "untenable".

However, since then, Nepal has signalled that it was willing to address the issue diplomatically. In the background, engagements continued.

advertisement

In June, the chairperson of Balen Shah's Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP), Rabi Lamichhane, received a high-profile and warm welcome in New Delhi. The next month, Shah broke his self-imposed protocol to meet Indian ambassador Naveen Srivastava.

WHAT'S BEHIND NEPAL PM'S TURNAROUND?

And then, flash floods struck Nepal. It left over 1,400 dead and 6,000 missing.

The flood, triggered by a glacial collapse in upstream Tibet, swept through parts of the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, swallowing towns, roads and bridges.

India acted swiftly to rush over hundreds of tonnes of emergency relief material and equipment like Bailey bridges to restore connectivity to far-flung areas. New Delhi also dispatched tunnelling experts and rescue teams to help workers stranded inside tunnels at hydropower projects.

According to the MEA, India rushed over 140 tonnes of relief material between August 26 and September 19, reinforcing its 'first responder' image whenever its neighbours face a crisis.

India also came in praise from Balen Shah in his first address at the UNGA in New York in September. In fact, the Nepalese PM also proposed a Himalayan Climate Resilience Mechanism between Nepal, India and China to tackle climate-change-related disasters.

advertisement

The tone towards India had begun to change. Experts said there is also an important economic reason for Nepal to strengthen its ties with India.

Constantino Xavier, an expert on South Asian affairs, cited an economic angle behind the sudden shift in Nepal's approach.

"Nepal and other neighbours realise rising reliance on and benefits of closer economic relations with India to attain developmental objectives - especially given global slowdown and disruptions," Xavier, a visiting professor at Ashoka University, tweeted.

To buttress his point, he shared a news report from The Kathmandu Post that said Nepal has sought an economic package worth more than $2 billion (Rs 18,786 crore), comprising lines of credit and grants, from India.

The economic package came up for discussion during the meeting between Misri and Shah, the report said. A Nepal finance ministry official said an announcement is likely to be made during Shah's visit to India. There has been no statement from New Delhi.

Nepal said the funds would primarily be used to construct transmission lines and for reconstruction efforts following the flash floods.

THE GORKHA FACTOR

Crucially, Shah's move to pick India, and not China, for his first bilateral foreign visit indicates his eagerness to reshape ties with New Delhi.

advertisement

Another key irritant in India-Nepal ties has been the pause in the recruitment of Gorkha soldiers in the Indian Army following the Agnipath scheme. Under the scheme, introduced in 2022, only up to 25% of recruits would be retained for permanent service after four years.

This irked Nepal, which subsequently suspended the recruitment of Nepali youths in the Indian Army. It argued that the scheme was not in accordance with the 1947 tripartite agreement signed between India, Nepal and Britain.

However, earlier this week, India revamped the scheme to allow Agniveers undergoing training in the three services to join the forces as regular soldiers.

This is likely to create a more favourable environment for discussions on resuming the recruitment of Nepali Gorkhas. Coincidentally, the government move comes ahead of Balen Shah's visit.

For India, Nepal is a crucial piece in the regional security map. This is undeniable.

Five states - Bengal, Uttarakhand, UP, Bihar and Sikkim - share borders with Nepal. These are close to areas where Indian and Chinese interests overlap. Thus, for New Delhi, a Nepal that drifts too close to China will ring alarm bells.

For now, all eyes will be on Balen Shah's upcoming visit to New Delhi later this month. It will be the first visit by a Nepali PM in three years. The last visit happened in 2023, when then Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal travelled to New Delhi.

title: One-off aid of $3,100 for families of all 54 Malaysian victims in Nepal flood - The Straits Times
description: One-off aid of $3,100 for families of all 54 Malaysian victims in Nepal flood  The Straits Times
publisher.title: The Straits Times
full_article:
KUALA LUMPUR – All families of the 54 Malaysian victims of the Nepal flood tragedy in August will receive a one-off payment of RM10,000 (S$3,100) through Malaysia’s National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA).

Malaysia’s Human Resources Minister Ramanan Ramakrishnan said the matter was decided by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim after detailed discussions at the Cabinet meeting on Nov 6.

“We discussed it at length in the Cabinet, and the Prime Minister decided that a one-off payment of RM10,000 will be given to each victim’s family, but they must follow the list set out under NADMA.

“This means there is an order of priority. For example, the priority is the wife or husband, the second is the parents and the third is the children.

“We will issue the list,” he told reporters after visiting the 24th Deepavali Carnival 2026 at Bukit Jalil National Stadium in Kuala Lumpur on Nov 6.

Ramanan said he had directed the director-general of the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit, K. Raveendran Nair, to obtain detailed information from the Finance Ministry and to contact the victims’ next of kin soon.

The devastating flood and debris flow on Aug 26, triggered by a glacial ice and rock avalanche in the upper catchment area of Lhende Khola in Tibet, China, has so far claimed at least 1,450 lives.

About 5,700 individuals, including more than 600 foreign nationals, are still reported missing. BERNAMA

title: Nepal's Tax System Faces Major Overhaul as IMF Calls for Smarter Revenue Policies and Reforms - Devdiscourse
description: Nepal's Tax System Faces Major Overhaul as IMF Calls for Smarter Revenue Policies and Reforms  Devdiscourse
publisher.title: Devdiscourse
full_article:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF), through its Fiscal Affairs Department, has urged Nepal to strengthen its tax policymaking system, warning that weak institutional coordination, limited technical expertise and inadequate revenue analysis could undermine the country's efforts to improve government finances. In its 2026 report, Nepal: Building an Effective Revenue Policy Unit, prepared by IMF experts Li Liu, Rasmi Das and Michael Keen, the institution recommends major reforms to make taxation more transparent, predictable and evidence-based. The findings follow an IMF technical assistance mission to Kathmandu from March 30 to April 9, 2026, conducted at the request of Nepal's Ministry of Finance. The report highlights how stronger tax institutions could help the government increase domestic revenue, improve fiscal planning and make better-informed economic decisions.

Nepal's Tax Reform Ambitions Face Institutional Challenges

Nepal has introduced several initiatives to modernize its tax system and strengthen revenue collection. The Domestic Resource Mobilization Strategy, launched in 2024, provides a five-year framework for improving tax policies and administration. The High-Level Recommendation Committee on Tax System Reforms, commonly known as the Mallick Report, offers additional recommendations for medium-term reforms.

The government's 100-point agenda reinforces these commitments by prioritizing measures to reduce revenue leakage, improve tax administration and strengthen international cooperation. However, the IMF finds that progress remains uneven despite tax reform measures introduced during fiscal years 2024/25 and 2025/26.

One important achievement is the Ministry of Finance's Tax Expenditure Report, which highlights opportunities to improve transparency and review tax exemptions and concessions. Such preferential treatments reduce potential government revenue, making regular assessments necessary to determine whether they deliver sufficient economic and social benefits.

The IMF believes stronger evaluation of these concessions could help Nepal protect public resources while supporting a fairer and more efficient tax system.

New Revenue Policy Unit Could Transform Tax Decisions

A major concern identified by the IMF is the limited progress in making Nepal's Revenue Policy Unit operational. Established in November 2025, the unit represents an important step toward improving tax policy coordination. However, during the IMF assessment, its responsibilities, institutional position and long-term functions remained unclear.

The report warns that simply creating a new government office will not improve taxation unless it receives adequate authority, skilled personnel and clear responsibilities.

Nepal's existing tax policymaking process is largely reactive, with decisions frequently developed under tight budget deadlines. The Revenue Advisory Committee, which oversees tax-related budget proposals, meets mainly during the annual budget cycle. This leaves insufficient time for consultation, detailed economic assessments and consideration of alternative policies.

The IMF also identifies limited analysis of how proposed tax changes would affect government revenue and different income groups. Unbalanced stakeholder representation and potential conflicts of interest further weaken the existing process.

To address these problems, the IMF recommends establishing a permanent, high-level Revenue Strategy Group to guide the Revenue Policy Unit. The unit would provide technical analysis, develop reform options and support government decisions. Eventually, it could become a division reporting directly to the Revenue Secretary.

Better Data, Skilled Experts and Forecasting Are Essential

The IMF emphasizes that Nepal must invest in professional expertise to build an effective tax policy institution. The Revenue Policy Unit would require economists, statisticians, data analysts, accountants, legal specialists and professionals familiar with Nepal's tax and customs systems.

Recruitment should prioritize technical competence, supported by continuous training and stronger cooperation between government departments. Access to anonymized taxpayer-level data would also help officials understand the effects of proposed tax measures.

The report identifies three immediate priorities. First, the unit should develop reliable revenue forecasts to improve fiscal planning. Second, it should strengthen tax expenditure analysis to evaluate the costs and benefits of exemptions and concessions. Both functions should become operational within the unit's first year.

Third, the unit should build its ability to provide evidence-based policy advice. Analytical tools already supplied by the IMF could help assess proposed changes to value-added tax and personal income tax, including their potential revenue and distributional effects.

Developing key tax indicators would further strengthen the government's ability to monitor tax performance and evaluate reforms.

What Stronger Tax Policies Mean for Businesses and Households

The IMF recommends restructuring the Revenue Advisory Committee into a government-only decision-making body while allowing independent experts, academics, civil society organizations and private-sector representatives to contribute through structured consultations.

These discussions should begin before mid-January, giving policymakers more time to evaluate proposals before budget decisions are finalized.

For businesses and traders, better-designed tax policies could improve predictability, reduce uncertainty and support investment planning. Earlier consultations could also help policymakers understand the practical challenges businesses face when complying with taxation requirements.

For consumers and households, stronger distributional analysis could help authorities assess whether proposed tax changes place disproportionate burdens on particular income groups.

For policymakers, improved forecasting and more transparent evaluation of tax concessions could support better fiscal decisions. International development partners could contribute through technical assistance, training and institutional capacity building.

Ultimately, the IMF's message is that Nepal needs more than ambitious tax reform commitments. Building a capable Revenue Policy Unit, strengthening consultation and using reliable economic evidence will be essential to improving domestic revenue mobilization and creating a more transparent, effective and sustainable tax system.
